title: Stochastic Voronoi Ensembles for Anomaly Detection
Stochastic Voronoi Ensembles for Anomaly Detection
summary: Anomaly detection methods struggle with data exhibiting varying local densities, where distance-based methods miss local anomalies and density-based methods require careful parameter selection and incur quadratic time complexity. SVEAD constructs an ensemble of random Voronoi diagrams by sampling anchors, scores points by normalized cell-relative distance weighted by local scale, and averages scores across partitions. Across 45 ADBench datasets it achieves the highest average AUC-ROC (0.8538) and AUC-PR (0.5000) among 12 baselines, including 0.9339 AUC-ROC on cardio, while maintaining linear time and constant space complexity.

approach: Route is paper_only with no author repository on disk (only an uncloned anonymous.4open.science link), so SVEAD is reimplemented from the paper: for each of t=100 partitions, sample m anchors uniformly without replacement, assign every point to its nearest anchor in standardized feature space (implicit Voronoi, no cell boundaries), score each point as (delta/delta_max) * delta_mean inside its cell, skip singleton cells, and average the per-partition scores. The match target is C1: AUC-ROC 0.9339 on ADBench cardio (1831 samples, 21 features, 176 anomalies); the dataset is fetched at runtime through a validated fallback chain (ADBench GitHub raw -> OpenML cardiotocography -> UCI Cardiotocography), all of which reduce to exactly the same 1831x21 table with 176 positives, and a hard validation gate asserts that shape before any scoring. The m hyperparameter is grid-searched over {2,4,...,256} with 5 seeded repeats per value and t=100, matching the paper's protocol (R7, R8); we report both the label-tuned best m and the full m-curve so the +/-0.0189 tolerance band is interpretable, plus AUC-PR (C2) for free from the same runs. C3/C4 (45 datasets) and C5/C6 (GPU 500k-instance scalability) are explicitly out of scope on this CPU-only machine and are flagged as 'not reproduced' in the output.
steps: Install/verify deps: `pip install numpy scipy pandas scikit-learn matplotlib requests tqdm openpyxl xlrd`; confirm sklearn.datasets.fetch_openml and sklearn.metrics imports succeed.

Write svead/data.py with a priority loader and an on-disk cache at data/cardio.npz: (1) local cache; (2) ADBench GitHub — GET https://api.github.com/repos/Minqi824/ADBench/git/trees/main?recursive=1, find any path containing 'cardio' ending in .csv/.npz/.arff, download via raw.githubusercontent.com; (3) sklearn.datasets.fetch_openml(data_id=1466) or name='cardiotocography' — take the 21 feature columns, keep rows with NSP in {1,3}, label = (NSP == 3); (4) UCI fallback https://archive.ics.uci.edu/static/public/193/cardiotocography.zip -> CTG.xls, same 21-feature/NSP filter.

Validate the loaded table in svead/data.py: assert X.shape == (1831, 21), y.sum() == 176, mean(y) ~= 0.0961, no NaN/inf (assumption A6); if any assertion fails on a fallback source, log the mismatch into the provenance dict and continue, because the source is then not guaranteed to be the ADBench cardio table.

Write svead/svead_core.py: sample_anchors(X, m, rng) -> unique row indices (R1); assign_cells(X, A, chunk_rows) -> (cell_ids, delta) using chunked Euclidean distance and argmin with lowest-index tie-break (R2, R11); cell_stats -> per-cell delta_max and delta_mean computed for all points before any scoring (R4); score_partition -> s = (delta / delta_max) * delta_mean with NaN for singleton cells and a delta_max == 0 guard (R3, R5); svead_score(X, m, t, seed) -> nanmean over t partitions, 0 if all NaN, plus diagnostics (cell-size histogram, skipped fraction, per-partition seconds) (R6, R12).

Write svead/metrics.py: roc_auc_score wrapper, average_precision_score (primary AUC-PR), trapezoidal precision_recall_curve AUC (secondary), and summarize(list) -> mean/std/min/max; all functions take scores first and labels second so labels are consumed only post-prediction (R9, R10).

Run the smoke test: `python experiments/smoke_test.py`. Part A: synthetic 300x6 with 10% Gaussian outliers, m=4, t=3 -> assert finite non-negative scores, shape (300,), AUC-ROC > 0.8. Part B: real cardio, m=8, t=5 -> assert score shape (1831,), deterministic repeat for the same seed, total runtime < 60 s.

Run the pre-full-run intermediate checks below (dataset signature, standardization stats, anchor uniqueness, cell-size/skip diagnostics, a kNN-distance and IsolationForest sanity baseline, single-run timing extrapolation).

Write experiments/run_cardio.py: outer loop over m in the 8-value grid, inner loop over the 5 seeds, each run calling svead_score on the standardized matrix with t=100, recording AUC-ROC, AUC-PR (both variants), wall time, skipped-point fraction and cell statistics; append rows to results/per_m_table.csv and dump raw per-run records to results/raw_cardio.json.

Launch the full suite: `python experiments/run_cardio.py`; after the first two m values finish, check that the extrapolated total stays inside the budget (expected total is only a few minutes because the per-run cost is ~0.1-3 s at these sizes) and only then let it complete.

Select best m = argmax of mean AUC-ROC across the 5 seeds; compute mean/std for AUC-ROC and AUC-PR at that m, and also record the fixed-m=128 (A3 fallback) result and the full m-curve for sensitivity.

Write reproduce.py: load data from cache, reuse or regenerate results/raw_cardio.json, run selection, then write results/metrics.json with (a) C1 value vs 0.9339 with the 0.0189 band and PASS/FAIL verdict, (b) C2 value vs 0.5356, (c) per-m table and per-repeat spreads, (d) dataset provenance and validation flags, (e) timing, (f) the assumption ledger entries applied, (g) an explicit not_reproduced block for C3, C4, C5 and C6 (45-dataset average and GPU/500k scalability are out of scope on CPU).

Run the final entrypoint `python reproduce.py` and read results/metrics.json; report the reproduced C1 with its spread, label the overall verdict partially_reproduced, and never present C3-C6 as reproduced.
smoke_test: `python experiments/smoke_test.py` — synthesizes 300x6 data with 10% outliers at m=4, t=3 and asserts finite non-negative scores, shape (300,), AUC-ROC > 0.8; then scores the full 1831x21 cardio table at m=8, t=5, asserting shape (1831,), reproducible scores for a repeated seed, and under 60 s wall clock. This exercises download -> standardize -> anchor sampling -> nearest-anchor assignment -> cell stats -> scoring -> averaging -> AUC end to end on a few seconds of compute.
intermediate_checks: Dataset signature: X.shape == (1831, 21), y.sum() == 176, anomaly rate 0.0961, zero NaN/inf, and the 21 UCI/ADBench feature names present — abort or flag loudly if a fallback source yields different counts (e.g. 2126 rows means the suspect class was not filtered).
Standardization: after StandardScaler, per-column mean ~ 0 (|mean| < 1e-9) and std ~ 1 for all 21 columns; confirm the scaler is fit with no label access.
Anchor sampling: for every m in the grid and every seed, sampled anchor indices are distinct and len == m (requirement R1), verified on 20 random (m, seed) pairs.

Cell diagnostics: for m=256 on n=1831, singleton cells must be essentially zero and skipped-point fraction < 0.5%; log non-empty cell count, max/mean cell size, and skipped fraction for every (m, seed).

Score sanity: all scores finite and >= 0; distribution roughly right-skewed with a handful of large scores matching injected/synthetic outliers; Spearman correlation with a trivial 1-NN mean-distance baseline is clearly positive.

Sanity baselines on cardio: sklearn IsolationForest(n_estimators=100, random_state=1) and a global kNN mean-distance score; both should land roughly in 0.65-0.85 AUC-ROC — if SVEAD cannot beat them, the reimplementation is wrong, not the paper.
No-cell-means-0 check: with the chosen cell_stats_scope (anchor included at distance 0), delta_mean must still be > 0 for every non-singleton cell; assert this before the full run.

Timing probe: time one full run at m=256, t=100 -> extrapolate the whole 40-run grid; if the extrapolation exceeds ~25 minutes, drop to 3 repeats and/or m in {8,16,32,64,128} (documented as a reduced protocol).
Determinism: two back-to-back runs with identical (m, seed) produce bitwise-identical score vectors.
budget_plan: Total ~90 min on CPU. Setup and data acquisition 15 min (pip installs, the ADBench/OpenML/UCI fallback chain, cache write, dataset-signature validation). Implementation of svead/data.py, svead/svead_core.py and svead/metrics.py 20 min. Smoke test and intermediate checks 10 min (including the IsolationForest/kNN sanity baselines and the timing probe). Full cardio grid 25 min reserved though expected ~5-10 min (8 m values x 5 seeds x t=100 on a 1831x21 matrix; each run is only a few seconds, so sum over m of m makes the whole grid roughly 2x the cost of a single m=256 run per seed). Final reproduce.py + metrics.json writing and interpretation 10 min. Contingency: if a run ever exceeds the projection, first cut repeats from 5 to 3, then narrow the m grid to four values, always recording the reduced protocol in results/metrics.json. C3/C4 (45 datasets) and C5/C6 (500k-instance CPU/GPU timing) are deliberately not scheduled.

"""Cardio dataset loading (ADBench).

Sources, tried in order (first one that validates wins):
  1. local workspace cache  data/cardio.npz
  2. shared REPRO_DATA_CACHE  (6_cardio.npz / cardio.npz / cardio_adbench.npz)
  3. ADBench GitHub (Minqi824/ADBench) raw npz, located through the git-tree API
  4. sklearn.datasets.fetch_openml(data_id=1466, "cardiotocography")
  5. UCI archive https://archive.ics.uci.edu/static/public/193/cardiotocography.zip

All of these reduce to the same 1831 x 21 table (NSP in {1,3}, label = NSP == 3,
176 anomalies, 9.61%).  The ADBench npz stores already-standardised features
(per-column mean ~0, std ~0.9997); we do *not* re-scale, because a global linear
rescale cannot change Euclidean nearest-anchor assignments and every metric used
here is invariant to a positive monotone rescaling of a single score vector.
No label is ever used for scoring (R10); labels are only returned for metrics.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import io
import json
import os
import urllib.request
import zipfile

import numpy as np

CACHE_DIR = os.environ.get("REPRO_DATA_CACHE", os.path.join("data"))
WORKSPACE_CACHE = os.path.join("data", "cardio.npz")
EXPECTED = {"n": 1831, "d": 21, "n_anomalies": 176}

ADBENCH_RAW = (
    "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Minqi824/ADBench/main/"
    "adbench/datasets/Classical/6_cardio.npz"
)
ADBENCH_TREE = (
    "https://api.github.com/repos/Minqi824/ADBench/git/trees/main?recursive=1"
)
UCI_ZIP = "https://archive.ics.uci.edu/static/public/193/cardiotocography.zip"


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# helpers
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def _http_get(url: str, timeout: int = 60) -> bytes:
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": "svead-repro/1.0"})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=timeout) as fh:
        return fh.read()


def _signature(X: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray) -> dict:
    return {
        "n": int(X.shape[0]),
        "d": int(X.shape[1]) if X.ndim == 2 else 0,
        "n_anomalies": int(y.sum()),
        "anomaly_rate": float(y.mean()),
    }


def _check(X, y, source: str, provenance: dict) -> bool:
    sig = _signature(X, y)
    provenance.setdefault("attempts", []).append({"source": source, "signature": sig})
    ok = (
        sig["n"] == EXPECTED["n"]
        and sig["d"] == EXPECTED["d"]
        and sig["n_anomalies"] == EXPECTED["n_anomalies"]
    )
    return ok


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# individual loaders -> (X, y) or None
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def _from_npz(path: str):
    if not os.path.isfile(path):
        return None
    try:
        d = np.load(path, allow_pickle=True)
    except Exception:
        return None
    if "X" not in d or "y" not in d:
        return None
    X = np.asarray(d["X"], dtype=np.float64)
    y = np.asarray(d["y"]).ravel()
    y = (y != 0).astype(int) if set(np.unique(y)) <= {0, 1, -1, True, False} else y.astype(int)
    if X.ndim != 2 or X.shape[0] != y.shape[0]:
        return None
    return X, y


def _parse_adbench_tree(tree_json: bytes):
    tree = json.loads(tree_json.decode("utf-8"))
    hits = []
    for node in tree.get("tree", []):
        p = node.get("path", "")
        if "cardio" in p.lower() and p.lower().endswith((".npz", ".csv", ".arff")):
            hits.append(p)
    return hits


def _download_adbench(cache_path: str):
    # direct raw URL first
    try:
        blob = _http_get(ADBENCH_RAW)
        with open(cache_path, "wb") as fh:
            fh.write(blob)
        return _from_npz(cache_path)
    except Exception:
        pass
    # otherwise find the file in the repository tree
    try:
        hits = _parse_adbench_tree(_http_get(ADBENCH_TREE))
    except Exception:
        return None
    for p in hits:
        try:
            url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Minqi824/ADBench/main/" + p
            blob = _http_get(url)
            if p.lower().endswith(".npz"):
                tmp = cache_path
                with open(tmp, "wb") as fh:
                    fh.write(blob)
                got = _from_npz(tmp)
                if got is not None:
                    return got
    except Exception:
        return None
    return None


def _download_openml():
    from sklearn.datasets import fetch_openml

    for kwargs in ({"data_id": 1466}, {"name": "cardiotocography"}):
        try:
            ds = fetch_openml(**kwargs, as_frame=True)
            df = ds.frame
            cols = [c for c in df.columns if c != "NSP"]
            X = df[cols].to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)
            nsp = df["NSP"].to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)
            keep = np.isin(nsp, [1, 3])
            X = X[keep]
            y = (nsp[keep] == 3).astype(int)
            return X, y
        except Exception:
            continue
    return None


def _download_uci():
    try:
        blob = _http_get(UCI_ZIP, timeout=120)
        zf = zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(blob))
        name = [n for n in zf.namelist() if n.lower().endswith((".xls", ".xlsx", ".csv"))]
        if not name:
            return None
        raw = zf.read(name[0])
        import pandas as pd

        if name[0].lower().endswith(".csv"):
            df = pd.read_csv(io.BytesIO(raw))
        else:
            df = pd.read_excel(io.BytesIO(raw))
        df.columns = [str(c).strip() for c in df.columns]
        nsp_col = [c for c in df.columns if c.upper() == "NSP"][0]
        num = df.select_dtypes(include=[np.number]).columns
        cols = [c for c in num if c != nsp_col]
        X = df[cols].to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)
        nsp = df[nsp_col].to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)
        keep = np.isin(nsp, [1, 3])
        return X[keep], (nsp[keep] == 3).astype(int)
    except Exception:

"""Core SVEAD implementation (reimplemented from the paper, no author code available).

Implements, with requirement ids from the claim contract:

* R1  sample_anchors            -- m points sampled uniformly without replacement
* R2  assign_cells              -- nearest anchor (Euclidean) = implicit Voronoi
* R11 assign_cells              -- no explicit cell boundaries/vertices
* R3  score_partition           -- s = (delta / delta_max) * delta_mean
* R4  cell_statistics           -- delta_max and delta_mean computed per cell
* R5  score_partition           -- |C| == 1 -> this point is skipped in this partition
* R6  svead_score               -- ensemble aggregation by arithmetic mean over t
* R12 chunked cdist              -- O(n*m*d*t) time, O(n) temporary space

Ensemble aggregation detail (assumption A12): the paper's Section 4.2 says a point
skipped in one partition "relies on the other t-1 partitions in the ensemble
average", while Algorithm 1 line 20 literally divides the accumulated sum by t.
Both variants are produced in a single pass and reported; the primary variant is
the Section 4.2 one (divide by the number of partitions that actually scored the
point).  They are identical whenever no point is skipped, which is the case for
all m values used here.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import time

import numpy as np
from scipy.spatial.distance import cdist

DEFAULT_CHUNK_ROWS = 4096


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# R1: anchor sampling
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def sample_anchors(n: int, m: int, rng: np.random.Generator) -> np.ndarray:
    """Sample m distinct row indices uniformly without replacement."""
    if m > n:
        raise ValueError(f"m={m} exceeds n={n}")
    return np.sort(rng.choice(n, size=m, replace=False))


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# R2 / R11 / R4: assignment and per-cell statistics
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def assign_cells(X: np.ndarray, A: np.ndarray, chunk_rows: int = DEFAULT_CHUNK_ROWS):
    """Assign every point to its nearest anchor.

    Returns (cell_ids, delta) where delta[i] = ||X[i] - A[cell_ids[i]]||.
    Ties are broken towards the lowest anchor index (numpy argmin convention).
    """
    n = X.shape[0]
    cell = np.empty(n, dtype=np.int32)
    delta = np.empty(n, dtype=np.float64)
    for s in range(0, n, chunk_rows):
        e = min(s + chunk_rows, n)
        D = cdist(X[s:e], A, metric="euclidean")
        idx = D.argmin(axis=1)
        cell[s:e] = idx
        delta[s:e] = D[np.arange(e - s), idx]
    return cell, delta


def cell_statistics(cell: np.ndarray, delta: np.ndarray, m: int):
    """R4: per-cell delta_max and delta_mean (anchor included, distance 0)."""
    sizes = np.bincount(cell, minlength=m).astype(np.int64)
    dmax = np.zeros(m, dtype=np.float64)
    dsum = np.zeros(m, dtype=np.float64)
    np.maximum.at(dmax, cell, delta)
    np.add.at(dsum, cell, delta)
    with np.errstate(invalid="ignore", divide="ignore"):
        dmean = np.where(sizes > 0, dsum / np.maximum(sizes, 1), 0.0)
    return sizes, dmax, dmean

# R3 / R5: per-partition scoring
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #

"""Full cardio protocol for SVEAD (paper Section 5.1).

For every m in the paper's grid {2^1, ..., 2^8} and every repeat (5 seeds),
run SVEAD with ensemble size t=100 on the 1831x21 cardio table and record
AUC-ROC / AUC-PR plus diagnostics.

Writes:
  results/per_m_table.csv   -- one row per (m, repeat)
  results/raw_cardio.json   -- per-run records + per-m summary

Usage:
  python experiments/run_cardio.py [--ms 2,4,...] [--repeats 5] [--t 100]
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import json
import os
import statistics
import sys
import time

import numpy as np

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))

from svead.data import load_cardio  # noqa: E402
from svead.metrics import average_precision, pr_curve_auc, roc_auc  # noqa: E402
from svead.svead_core import svead_score  # noqa: E402

DEFAULT_MS = [2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256]


def run(ms=None, repeats=5, t=100, seeds=None, out_dir="results", verbose=True) -> dict:
    ms = DEFAULT_MS if ms is None else list(ms)
    seeds = list(range(1, repeats + 1)) if seeds is None else list(seeds)
    X, y, provenance = load_cardio()
    os.makedirs(out_dir, exist_ok=True)

    records = []
    per_m = {}
    for m in ms:
        rows = []
        for seed in seeds:
            t0 = time.perf_counter()
            res = svead_score(X, m=m, t=t, seed=seed)
            wall = time.perf_counter() - t0
            s = res["scores"]
            row = {
                "m": int(m),
                "seed": int(seed),
                "t": int(t),
                "auc_roc": roc_auc(s, y),
                "auc_pr": average_precision(s, y),
                "auc_pr_trapz": pr_curve_auc(s, y),
                "auc_roc_div_t": roc_auc(res["scores_div_t"], y),
                "auc_pr_div_t": average_precision(res["scores_div_t"], y),
                "wall_seconds": wall,
                "internal_seconds": res["diagnostics"]["seconds"],
                "skipped_fraction": res["diagnostics"]["mean_skipped_fraction"],
                "max_skipped_fraction": res["diagnostics"]["max_skipped_fraction"],
                "mean_cell_size": res["diagnostics"]["mean_cell_size"],
                "mean_max_cell_size": res["diagnostics"]["mean_max_cell_size"],
                "points_never_scored": res["diagnostics"]["points_never_scored"],
                "n_distinct_scores": int(len(np.unique(s))),
            }
            rows.append(row)
            records.append(row)
        aucs = [r["auc_roc"] for r in rows]
        prs = [r["auc_pr"] for r in rows]
        per_m[m] = {
            "m": int(m),
            "auc_roc_mean": float(np.mean(aucs)),
            "auc_roc_std": float(statistics.stdev(aucs)) if len(aucs) > 1 else 0.0,
            "auc_pr_mean": float(np.mean(prs)),
            "auc_pr_std": float(statistics.stdev(prs)) if len(prs) > 1 else 0.0,
            "wall_seconds_mean": float(np.mean([r["wall_seconds"] for r in rows])),
            "skipped_fraction_mean": float(np.mean([r["skipped_fraction"] for r in rows])),
            "seeds": [int(r["seed"]) for r in rows],
        }
        if verbose:
            print(
                f"  m={m:4d}  AUC-ROC={per_m[m]['auc_roc_mean']:.4f}"
                f"+-{per_m[m]['auc_roc_std']:.4f}  AUC-PR={per_m[m]['auc_pr_mean']:.4f}"
                f"+-{per_m[m]['auc_pr_std']:.4f}  ({per_m[m]['wall_seconds_mean']:.2f}s/run)"
            )

    csv_path = os.path.join(out_dir, "per_m_table.csv")
    with open(csv_path, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        writer = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=list(records[0].keys()))
        writer.writeheader()
        writer.writerows(records)

    best_m = max(per_m, key=lambda k: per_m[k]["auc_roc_mean"])
    payload = {
        "protocol": {
            "m_grid": ms,
            "repeats": len(seeds),
            "seeds": seeds,
            "t": int(t),
            "m_selection": "argmax over m of the mean AUC-ROC across the repeats",
            "dataset": "ADBench cardio (1831x21, 176 anomalies)",
        },
        "per_m": {str(k): v for k, v in per_m.items()},
        "best_m": int(best_m),
        "records": records,
        "provenance": provenance,
    }
    with open(os.path.join(out_dir, "raw_cardio.json"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        json.dump(payload, fh, indent=2, default=str)
    if verbose:
        print(f"  selected m = {best_m}")
    return payload


def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--ms", default=",".join(str(m) for m in DEFAULT_MS))
    ap.add_argument("--repeats", type=int, default=5)
    ap.add_argument("--t", type=int, default=100)
    ap.add_argument("--out-dir", default="results")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    ms = [int(x) for x in args.ms.split(",") if x]
    print(f"SVEAD cardio protocol: m in {ms}, t={args.t}, repeats={args.repeats}")
    run(ms=ms, repeats=args.repeats, t=args.t, out_dir=args.out_dir)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

def scalability_measure(n=500_000, d=10, m=2, t=T_ENSEMBLE, seed=1) -> dict:
    """Time the full SVEAD pipeline on a synthetic n x d dataset (claim C5)."""
    out = {"n": int(n), "d": int(d), "m": int(m), "t": int(t),
           "cpu_count": os.cpu_count()}
    rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
    X = rng.normal(size=(n, d))
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    res = svead_score(X, m=m, t=t, seed=seed)
    out["seconds"] = time.perf_counter() - t0
    out["points_never_scored"] = res["diagnostics"]["points_never_scored"]
    out["note"] = (
        "Synthetic standard-normal data (paper does not state the generator), full "
        "pipeline (t partitions incl. anchor sampling, assignment, cell stats and "
        "scoring), data generation excluded. Device-dependent measurement on this "
        "CPU; the paper's machine is an AMD Ryzen 9 9950X and C6 needs an RTX 4090 "
        "GPU which this machine does not have."
    )
    return out


def scalability_sweep(ns=(50_000, 100_000, 200_000, 500_000), d=10, ms=(2, 8),
                      t=T_ENSEMBLE, seed=1) -> dict:
    """Runtime versus n (the substance of Figure 5), for a couple of m values."""
    runs = []
    for m in ms:
        for n in ns:
            r = scalability_measure(n=n, d=d, m=m, t=t, seed=seed)
            runs.append(r)
            print(f"  n={n:>7d} m={m:>3d} t={t}: {r['seconds']:.2f} s")
    main = [r for r in runs if r["m"] == ms[0]]
    fit = {}
    if len(main) > 1:
        x = np.log([r["n"] for r in main])
        yv = np.log([r["seconds"] for r in main])
        fit = {
            "log_log_slope": float(np.polyfit(x, yv, 1)[0]),
            "note": "slope ~1 indicates the linear-in-n complexity of the method (R12)",
        }
    return {
        "sweep": runs,
        "n_values": list(ns),
        "d": d,
        "t": t,
        "m_values": list(ms),
        "primary": next(r for r in runs if r["n"] == max(ns) and r["m"] == ms[0]),
        "linearity_fit": fit,
        "seconds_at_500k_m2": next((r["seconds"] for r in runs

        "seconds_at_500k_m8": next((r["seconds"] for r in runs

requirement_check.evidence: sample_anchors() uses rng.choice(n, size=m, replace=False); intermediate_checks + smoke test verify m distinct indices across 20 random (m,seed) pairs.
assign_cells() computes cdist(X_chunk, A, 'euclidean') and takes argmin; points are assigned to the nearest anchor with no cell boundary construction.
score_partition(): numer = delta * dmean[cell]; denom = dmax[cell]; s = numer/denom = (delta/dmax)*dmean, matching the contract's (δ/δmax)*δmean reading of Eqs (2)-(3).
cell_statistics() computes per-cell dmax (np.maximum.at) and dmean (sum/size) from anchor distances before any scoring.
singleton = sizes[cell] == 1 -> score set to NaN and excluded from the partition average; metrics.json reports skipped fraction 0.0 at the selected m=2 (no point is ever lost).

svead_score() accumulates scores and divides by the number of partitions that actually scored the point; at m=2 count==t==100 for every point, so this is exactly the arithmetic mean over t partitions (the divide-by-t variant is also computed and identical).
M_GRID=[2,4,8,16,32,64,128,256] = {2^1..2^8}, t=100 fixed; the full m-grid search was run in the target run and the selected m=2 is logged in selected_config.json.
run_cardio.py loops seeds 1..5 (repeats=5) and reports the mean/std; c1_auc_roc.per_seed lists all five runs.
metrics.py uses sklearn roc_auc_score and average_precision_score (a trapezoidal PR-AUC is additionally reported as a secondary check).
All scoring code (svead_core) takes only X; y is passed in solely to the metric functions in metrics.py, which run after scores are produced.
Cell membership is computed purely through nearest-anchor argmin on distances; no Voronoi vertices/edges are ever generated.
cdist is chunked (4096 rows) so time is O(n*m*d*t) and temporary space is O(chunk*m); the 500k x 10 run with t=100 completed in 4.07 s, confirming linear-in-n scaling.
